sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: For centuries, physicians regarded fever as a dangerous disease, an enemy to be crushed.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，医生一直把发烧视为一种危险的疾病，是必须被消灭的敌人。

sentences.en: In ancient and medieval medicine, fever was thought to represent an excess of heat or humor in the blood,
sentences.zh: 在古代和中世纪的医学中，人们认为发烧代表着血液中热量或体液过剩，

sentences.en: a sign that the body's internal balance had gone dangerously askew.
sentences.zh: 这是身体内部平衡发生危险偏离的迹象。

sentences.en: Treatments aimed to drive out the heat.
sentences.zh: 治疗的目的是驱散热气。

sentences.en: Patients were bled, purged, or doused with cold water.
sentences.zh: 患者被放血、泻药治疗，或者用冷水泼洒。

sentences.en: Some were packed in ice or fed diets designed to cool the blood.
sentences.zh: 有些人被包裹在冰块中，或者被喂食旨在冷却血液的饮食。

sentences.en: Well into the 19th century, fever was still widely feared as a destructive force that could consume a person from within.
sentences.zh: 直到19世纪，发烧仍然被广泛恐惧为一种破坏性力量，能够从内部吞噬一个人。

sentences.en: Doctors prescribed mercury-based compounds, quinine, or alcohol in large quantities.
sentences.zh: 医生们开了大量含汞化合物、奎宁或酒精。

sentences.en: Patients were subjected to fever cures in which they were submerged in prolonged cold baths
sentences.zh: 患者接受发烧疗法，被浸泡在长时间的冷水浴中，

sentences.en: or were wrapped in vinegar-soaked sheets, all in the hope of forcing the body's temperature back down.
sentences.zh: 或者包裹在浸透醋的床单里，这一切都是为了迫使体温降下来。

sentences.en: It wasn't until the late 19th and early 20th centuries that scientists began to recognize fever not as a disease,
sentences.zh: 直到19世纪末和20世纪初，科学家们才开始认识到发烧不是一种疾病，

sentences.en: but as a natural response of the body's immune system.
sentences.zh: 而是身体免疫系统的自然反应。

sentences.en: Research showed that infections, not fever, were the real enemy.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，感染才是真正的敌人，而不是发烧。

sentences.en: Studies showed that moderate fever actually helped the body fight infection by slowing the growth of bacteria and enhancing immune function.
sentences.zh: 研究显示，中度发烧实际上通过减缓细菌生长和增强免疫功能来帮助身体对抗感染。

sentences.en: This shift marked a profound change in medical thinking.
sentences.zh: 这种转变标志着医学思想的深刻变革。

sentences.en: Instead of reflexively suppressing fever, physicians began to see it as evidence of the body's vitality and capacity for self-defense.
sentences.zh: 医生们没有条件反射般地抑制发烧，而是开始将其视为身体活力和自我防御能力的证据。

sentences.en: Today, while very high fevers are still considered dangerous and treated,
sentences.zh: 今天，虽然非常高的烧仍然被认为很危险并需要治疗，

sentences.en: mild to moderate fevers are often allowed to run their course,
sentences.zh: 但轻度到中度的发烧通常任其自然发展，

sentences.en: a quiet acknowledgement that what was once seen as a deadly illness
sentences.zh: 这是一种默许：曾经被视为致命疾病的东西，

sentences.en: is, in fact, a sign of the body's strength.
sentences.zh: 实际上是身体力量的象征。

sentences.en: Today on the show, we investigate the possibility that what is true of our physical health
sentences.zh: 今天在节目中，我们探讨这样一种可能性：我们身体健康的真相，

sentences.en: may also be true of our mental health.
sentences.zh: 可能也适用于我们的心理健康。

sentences.en: That even a scourge like depression may have its roots in our powerful drive to survive and flourish.
sentences.zh: 即便是抑郁症这样的大患，也可能根植于我们对生存和繁衍的强大驱动力之中。

sentences.en: A note that this story includes a discussion of suicide.
sentences.zh: 需要说明的是，本期节目包含关于自杀的讨论。

sentences.en: If you or someone you love is struggling with thoughts of suicide,
sentences.zh: 如果你或你爱的人正在与自杀念头作斗争，

sentences.en: there are people who can help.
sentences.zh: 有人可以提供帮助。

sentences.en: Call or text the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline at 988.
sentences.zh: 请拨打或发短信至自杀与危机生命热线988。

sentences.en: If you're outside the U.S., we've included a link in our episode notes
sentences.zh: 如果你在美国境外，我们在本期节目简介中附了一个链接，

sentences.en: where you can find mental health support in your country.
sentences.zh: 你可以在那里找到你所在国家的心理健康支持。

sentences.en: We live in a culture that prizes strength and confidence
sentences.zh: 我们生活在一个崇尚力量与自信、

sentences.en: and that celebrates happiness and high mood.
sentences.zh: 赞美快乐和高昂情绪的文化中。

sentences.en: So when those things slip away, when our energy disappears,
sentences.zh: 因此，当这些东西溜走，当我们的精力消失，

sentences.en: when joy goes missing,
sentences.zh: 当快乐不见踪影时，

sentences.en: we naturally assume that something must have gone very wrong.
sentences.zh: 我们自然会认为一定出了什么大问题。

sentences.en: We look for a problem to fix, a disease to cure.
sentences.zh: 我们寻找要解决的问题，要治愈的疾病。

sentences.en: At Cornell University, psychologist Jonathan Rottenberg has long asked
sentences.zh: 在康奈尔大学，心理学家乔纳森·罗滕伯格长期以来一直在问，

sentences.en: if this is the right way to think about depression.
sentences.zh: 这是否是思考抑郁症的正确方式。

sentences.en: John Rottenberg, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 约翰·罗滕伯格，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: It's wonderful to be here with you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能和你在一起。

sentences.en: Thirty years ago, John, you were a confident, self-assured college graduate
sentences.zh: 三十年前，约翰，你是一个自信满满的大学毕业生，

sentences.en: preparing to get married and to start a career.
sentences.zh: 正准备结婚并开始职业生涯。

sentences.en: What was your life like at the time and what were your plans for the future?
sentences.zh: 你当时的生活是怎样的？你对未来有什么计划？

sentences.en: I was studying.
sentences.zh: 我当时在学习。

sentences.en: I was in a Ph.D.
sentences.zh: 我在读博士，

sentences.en: program in history living in Baltimore at Johns Hopkins University.
sentences.zh: 历史专业，住在巴尔的摩的约翰斯·霍普金斯大学。

sentences.en: I studied American history and I thought I was the smartest guy in the room.
sentences.zh: 我研究美国历史，我以为自己是房间里最聪明的人。

sentences.en: And I was then struck by a series of very bizarre experiences
sentences.zh: 然后我遭遇了一系列非常诡异的经历，

sentences.en: that I had no framework for understanding.
sentences.zh: 我没有任何框架来理解它们。

sentences.en: Tell me what happened.
sentences.zh: 告诉我发生了什么。

sentences.en: In many ways, you had all of your life before you.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，你的人生还很漫长。

sentences.en: You had graduated from an Ivy League school.
sentences.zh: 你从常春藤盟校毕业。

sentences.en: You were about to get married.
sentences.zh: 你即将结婚。

sentences.en: You were doing this Ph.D.
sentences.zh: 你在攻读博士学位，

sentences.en: and you thought you were the smartest person in the room.
sentences.zh: 你以为自己是房间里最聪明的人。

sentences.en: It felt like everything was going your way.
sentences.zh: 感觉一切都对你有利。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so when I started to feel unwell,
sentences.zh: 所以当我开始感到不适时，

sentences.en: I didn't have really much of a framework to go on.
sentences.zh: 我真的没有太多框架可以依据。

sentences.en: I first noticed physical symptoms that didn't make a whole lot of sense.
sentences.zh: 我首先注意到了一些毫无道理的身体症状。

sentences.en: I had pain on the left side of my body.
sentences.zh: 我身体左侧感到疼痛。

sentences.en: I thought there might be something wrong with my heart.
sentences.zh: 我以为我的心脏可能出了问题。

sentences.en: I felt physically weak.
sentences.zh: 我觉得身体虚弱。

sentences.en: Like I thought I might have a fever or some kind of flu-like illness.
sentences.zh: 就像我以为自己发烧了或者得了某种流感样疾病。

sentences.en: I felt incredibly run down and I thought that it would just go away on its own.
sentences.zh: 我感到虚弱不堪，以为它会自己消失。

sentences.en: And then other problems started.
sentences.zh: 然后其他问题接踵而至。

sentences.en: So rather than it getting better, it got worse.
sentences.zh: 所以情况不仅没有好转，反而恶化了。

sentences.en: So what started to change was that my ability to focus, read, think,
sentences.zh: 开始发生变化的是我的专注力、阅读能力和思考能力，

sentences.en: that degenerated pretty rapidly.
sentences.zh: 这些能力退化得相当快。

sentences.en: So this tool that I used to understand the world,
sentences.zh: 所以我用来理解世界的这个工具，

sentences.en: this tool that really defined who I was,
sentences.zh: 这个真正定义了我是谁的工具，

sentences.en: my brain, my mind, was not working right.
sentences.zh: 我的大脑，我的心智，运作不正常了。

sentences.en: So here I am in a history program
sentences.zh: 所以当时我身处一个历史项目，

sentences.en: and I'm working on a dissertation and I can't read a book.
sentences.zh: 我正在写学位论文，却连一本书都读不下去。

sentences.en: I mean, I can look at a page and I see the words
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我看着一页纸，能看到字，

sentences.en: and my ability to concentrate is getting to be close to zero.
sentences.zh: 但我的注意力集中能力接近于零。

sentences.en: So I started to get scared.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始害怕了。

sentences.en: What could explain this?
sentences.zh: 这怎么解释？

sentences.en: So I was even more baffled and I felt like something terrible
sentences.zh: 所以我更加迷茫，觉得有什么可怕的事情

sentences.en: was happening to me, but I didn't know what it was.
sentences.zh: 正在发生在我身上，但我不知道那是什么。

sentences.en: At what point did this clarify itself?
sentences.zh: 这种情况是在哪个时间点变得清晰的？

sentences.en: At what point did doctors come up with a diagnosis, John?
sentences.zh: 医生们是在哪个时间点给出诊断的，约翰？

sentences.en: It took months.
sentences.zh: 花了好几个月。

sentences.en: I remember going home.
sentences.zh: 我记得我回了家。

sentences.en: I was living in Baltimore, driving home,
sentences.zh: 我住在巴尔的摩，开车回家，

sentences.en: and that was very difficult to Connecticut.
sentences.zh: 那段路开到康涅狄格州非常艰难。

sentences.en: And meeting with a psychiatrist who is a colleague of my father's.
sentences.zh: 然后去见了一位我父亲同事的精神病医生。

sentences.en: And I believe that colleague was the first person
sentences.zh: 我相信那位同事是第一个

sentences.en: to suggest that this might be depression.
sentences.zh: 暗示这可能是抑郁症的人。

sentences.en: And that rocked my world.
sentences.zh: 这震撼了我的世界。

sentences.en: The sensations I was experiencing
sentences.zh: 我体验到的感觉

sentences.en: were not what I understood to be the symptoms of depression,
sentences.zh: 并不是我所理解的抑郁症症状，

sentences.en: which were feeling sad or just losing interest in things.
sentences.zh: 即感到悲伤或对事物失去兴趣。

sentences.en: I was really more experiencing this terrible fatigue,
sentences.zh: 我实际上更多地体验到这种可怕的疲劳，

sentences.en: this inability to concentrate.
sentences.zh: 这种无法集中的状态。

sentences.en: And so I did get a referral to see a psychiatrist in Baltimore.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实拿到了转诊单去巴尔的摩看精神科医生。

sentences.en: And I was started on medication.
sentences.zh: 我开始服药。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, it didn't help me.
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，这对我没有帮助。

sentences.en: And I continued to struggle and become more and more distraught
sentences.zh: 我继续挣扎，对这种情况越来越痛苦，

sentences.en: over the situation and less and less functional.
sentences.zh: 功能也越来越受限。

sentences.en: So I was spending large parts of the day lying on the ground.
sentences.zh: 所以我一天中大部分时间都躺在地板上。

sentences.en: Well, for someone who was so proud of his own mind and how his mind worked,
sentences.zh: 好吧，对于一个如此为自己的心智及其运作方式感到骄傲的人来说，

sentences.en: I'm wondering if there was an element of shame
sentences.zh: 我想知道，在你经历这一切时，

sentences.en: that you felt as you were experiencing this.
sentences.zh: 是否也伴随着一种羞耻感。

sentences.en: Yes, I felt humiliated.
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得自己受到了羞辱。

sentences.en: And I felt completely like I didn't know who I was.
sentences.zh: 我完全觉得自己不知道我是谁了。

sentences.en: If I couldn't think that I had no reason for being.
sentences.zh: 如果我无法思考，我便失去了存在的理由。

sentences.en: I had no purpose in life.
sentences.zh: 我在生活中没有任何目标。

sentences.en: And it was very scary.
sentences.zh: 这非常可怕。

sentences.en: And the fact that the treatment did not initially help me made it worse.
sentences.zh: 最初的治疗没有帮助，这让情况变得更糟。

sentences.en: And I had support of my then-girlfriend.
sentences.zh: 我有当时的女友的支持。

sentences.en: And she stayed with me.
sentences.zh: 她留在我身边。

sentences.en: But I became more and more difficult to be around.
sentences.zh: 但我变得越来越难相处。

sentences.en: I became more emotionally volatile.
sentences.zh: 我的情绪变得更加不稳定。

sentences.en: I spent hours and hours crying.
sentences.zh: 我花了几个小时又几个小时地哭泣。

sentences.en: I started to experience suicidal fantasies of not wanting to be alive
sentences.zh: 我开始产生自杀的幻想，不想活下去，

sentences.en: or even believing that I simply wouldn't have a future.
sentences.zh: 甚至相信自己根本不会有未来。

sentences.en: It became more and more difficult for me to imagine that I would have a future.
sentences.zh: 我越来越难以想象自己会有未来。

sentences.en: I didn't see myself as ever being able to emerge from this
sentences.zh: 我甚至不觉得自己能够摆脱困境，

sentences.en: because the depression felt like it was bigger than me.
sentences.zh: 因为抑郁症感觉比我更宏大。

sentences.en: It was stronger than me.
sentences.zh: 它比我更坚强。

sentences.en: It was more powerful than me.
sentences.zh: 它比我更有力量。

sentences.en: And that was a horrible feeling of powerlessness.
sentences.zh: 那是一种可怕的无力感。

sentences.en: I'm wondering how you viewed your future at this time, John.
sentences.zh: 约翰，我想知道你当时是如何看待你的未来的。

sentences.en: Did the path that seemed so bright some months earlier,
sentences.zh: 几个月前看起来还那么光明的道路，

sentences.en: did it seem that it had closed off for you?
sentences.zh: 对你来说是不是已经彻底关闭了？

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全关闭了。

sentences.en: By this point, I had gone on leave from my history program.
sentences.zh: 到了这个时候，我已经向历史专业请假了。

sentences.en: I had told my advisor that I was probably not coming back to the program,
sentences.zh: 我告诉我的导师我可能不会回去了，

sentences.en: which was very, very difficult.
sentences.zh: 这非常非常艰难。

sentences.en: And the path forward was very unclear.
sentences.zh: 前方的道路非常模糊。

sentences.en: I knew that I was somehow continuing with my relationship with Laura,
sentences.zh: 我知道我某种程度上还在和劳拉维持着恋爱关系，

sentences.en: which was incredible that she was staying with me.
sentences.zh: 她能留在我身边真是不可思议。

sentences.en: But I wasn't sure that I was going to make it to the other side.
sentences.zh: 但我并不确定自己能否熬过去。

sentences.en: I really had a lot of doubt that I was going to make it to the other side.
sentences.zh: 我真的很怀疑自己能不能熬过去。

sentences.en: And I was at my limit.
sentences.zh: 我达到了极限。

sentences.en: Every day, I felt I was at my absolute limit of what I could possibly bear.
sentences.zh: 每天，我都觉得自己达到了我所能承受的绝对极限。

sentences.en: I thought that no person, no person can bear this.
sentences.zh: 我想没有人，没有人能承受这个。

sentences.en: I mean, I felt completely obliterated.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我感觉自己彻底灰飞烟灭了。

sentences.en: How long did your depression last, John?
sentences.zh: 约翰，你的抑郁症持续了多久？

sentences.en: And how did it finally come to an end?
sentences.zh: 它又是如何最终结束的？

sentences.en: It lasted, I guess you could say, four years.
sentences.zh: 我想可以说，它持续了四年。

sentences.en: And it involved my really dedicating myself and sinking myself into the study of psychology
sentences.zh: 这期间我真正全身心投入到心理学研究中，

sentences.en: and into the study of mood disorders.
sentences.zh: 投入到情绪障碍的研究中。

sentences.en: I applied to graduate school.
sentences.zh: 我申请了研究生院。

sentences.en: I thought maybe I can rehabilitate myself.
sentences.zh: 我想也许我可以重塑自我。

sentences.en: Maybe I can rehabilitate my mind.
sentences.zh: 也许我可以修复我的心智。

sentences.en: And miraculously, I was admitted to a PhD program,
sentences.zh: 奇迹般地，我被一个博士项目录取了，

sentences.en: actually a really tremendous PhD program at Stanford University.
sentences.zh: 实际上，斯坦福大学的博士项目真的很棒。

sentences.en: And that was where my wife's family was from.
sentences.zh: 而且我妻子就是那儿的人。

sentences.en: And so she was overjoyed.
sentences.zh: 所以她高兴极了。

sentences.en: By that point, we were married and expecting a child.
sentences.zh: 到那时，我们已经结婚并怀上了孩子。

sentences.en: So there were things I could imagine that there were things to live for,
sentences.zh: 所以我想象生活中还是有值得期待的东西的，

sentences.en: even if I felt like I was faking it every day.
sentences.zh: 哪怕我感觉自己每天都在强颜欢笑。

sentences.en: I was still struggling to concentrate.
sentences.zh: 我当时依然很难集中注意力。

sentences.en: I did not feel confident in my ability to do this PhD program.
sentences.zh: 我对完成这个博士项目的能力感到很没有信心。

sentences.en: But I was going to try.
sentences.zh: 但我还是决定试一试。

sentences.en: And the idea that I would have the opportunity to understand depression,
sentences.zh: 而且，一想到我有机会去理解抑郁症，

sentences.en: it felt like, in my heart, my only chance.
sentences.zh: 我心里就觉得，这是我唯一的生路了。

sentences.en: I think it was enough to gradually move me in the direction that I needed to be.
sentences.zh: 我想，这足以慢慢推动我朝着我需要去的方向前进了。

sentences.en: And I sort of returned to the land of the living.
sentences.zh: 我算是重新回到了正常生活的轨道。

sentences.en: But it was a gradual process.
sentences.zh: 但这却是一个缓慢的过程。

sentences.en: When John Rottenberg first fell into a severe depression,
sentences.zh: 当约翰·罗滕伯格第一次陷入严重抑郁时，

sentences.en: he saw it through a particular lens.
sentences.zh: 他是带着一种特殊的视角来看待它的。

sentences.en: Like many of us, he had absorbed the notion that depression was a flaw in character
sentences.zh: 和我们许多人一样，他曾接受过这样一种观点：抑郁症是性格上的缺陷，

sentences.en: or in brain chemistry.
sentences.zh: 或者是大脑化学物质上的缺陷。

sentences.en: It took years for him to see his experience in a different light.
sentences.zh: 他花了多年时间，才以一种不同的眼光来看待自己的经历。

sentences.en: That's when we come back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: For several decades now, we've been told that depression is a malfunction,
sentences.zh: 几十年来，人们一直告诉我们，抑郁症是一种机能失常，

sentences.en: a glitch in our brain chemistry, a flaw in our cognitive wiring.
sentences.zh: 是我们大脑化学物质的一个小故障，是我们认知神经回路上的一个瑕疵。

sentences.en: But at Cornell University, psychologist John Rottenberg says this account may be wrong,
sentences.zh: 但在康奈尔大学，心理学家约翰·罗滕伯格却表示，这种说法可能是错误的，

sentences.en: or at least incomplete.
sentences.zh: 或者至少是不全面的。

sentences.en: John, how would you describe the prevailing model that we have of depression?
sentences.zh: 约翰，你将我们对抑郁症的普遍认知模式描述为怎样的？

sentences.en: The prevailing model that we have of depression is that depression reflects some fundamental defect
sentences.zh: 我们对抑郁症的普遍认知模式是，抑郁症反映了某种根本性的缺陷，

sentences.en: that is inside the depressed person.
sentences.zh: 这种缺陷就存在于抑郁症患者的体内。

sentences.en: That defect might be in the person's mind, like the way that the person thinks.
sentences.zh: 这种缺陷可能存在于人的思想中，比如一个人的思考方式。

sentences.en: Or that defect might be in the person's brain, like in the chemicals that are circulating between the neurons.
sentences.zh: 或者这种缺陷可能存在于人的大脑中，比如神经元之间循环的化学物质。

sentences.en: Or that defect might be in how the person is interacting with other people.
sentences.zh: 或者这种缺陷可能存在于人与其他人互动的方式中。

sentences.en: But in the final analysis, the reason that people are depressed is that they have some fundamental defect
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，人们之所以会抑郁，是因为他们的体内存在某种根本性的缺陷，

sentences.en: or defects inside themselves that explain why they are subject to episode or repeated episodes of depression.
sentences.zh: 或者多种缺陷，这解释了为什么他们会遭受单次或反复发作的抑郁。

sentences.en: You say that the defect model often blames depression on faulty brain chemistry
sentences.zh: 你说缺陷模型常常把抑郁症归咎于大脑化学物质失常，

sentences.en: and claims that antidepressants are the solution, but that the evidence doesn't fully support this idea.
sentences.zh: 并声称抗抑郁药是解决方案，但证据并不完全支持这一观点。

sentences.en: How so, John?
sentences.zh: 为什么这么说，约翰？

sentences.en: People have been studying the biological contributions to depression for 50, 60, 70 years.
sentences.zh: 人们研究抑郁症的生物学成因已经有50、60、70年了。

sentences.en: And I do believe that part of depression involves biological factors,
sentences.zh: 而且我确实相信，抑郁症的一部分原因涉及生物学因素，

sentences.en: but that's very different from saying that there is a biological cause, a single cause in the brain.
sentences.zh: 但这与说存在一个生物学成因、大脑中的单一成因是完全不同的概念。

sentences.en: And the search for antidepressants has led to a large number of therapies.
sentences.zh: 对抗抑郁药的搜寻已经催生了大量的疗法。

sentences.en: There's over 20 different antidepressants, but none of them could be called a cure.
sentences.zh: 有20多种不同的抗抑郁药，但没有一种能被称为是治愈的良药。

sentences.en: And I do think it's a bit misleading, this metaphor that's often used to talk about a chemical imbalance,
sentences.zh: 而且我确实认为，这种常用来谈论化学失衡的比喻有点误导性，

sentences.en: because that imbalance has never been isolated.
sentences.zh: 因为这种失衡从未被真正分离出来过。

sentences.en: It's never been fully characterized.
sentences.zh: 它从未被完整地描述过。

sentences.en: It can't be measured.
sentences.zh: 它也无法被测量。

sentences.en: And so what you have are treatments which are useful for many people, but it relies on a metaphor.
sentences.zh: 所以你所拥有的只是对许多人有用的治疗方法，但它是建立在一个比喻之上的。

sentences.en: When a patient comes in and wants help, the physician or psychiatrist might tell them that they have a chemical imbalance,
sentences.zh: 当患者进来寻求帮助时，内科医生或精神科医生可能会告诉他们存在化学失衡，

sentences.en: but the problem is you can't present to them their number, and you can't show that the treatment is changing that number.
sentences.zh: 但问题在于，你无法向他们展示他们的具体数值，你也无法证明治疗正在改变这个数值。

sentences.en: So you're really engaging in hand-waving, and I don't think that's doing a full service to our level of knowledge
sentences.zh: 所以这其实是在夸夸其谈，我认为这并没有完全尽到我们知识水平应尽的责任，

sentences.en: and being fully candid with people who are really struggling.
sentences.zh: 也没有对那些真正苦苦挣扎的人做到完全坦诚。

sentences.en: So this would be in contrast to something like, you know, if a physician worries that you have high cholesterol,
sentences.zh: 所以，这就像是，你知道的，如果医生担心你胆固醇高，

sentences.en: you can take a blood test and actually show what your cholesterol levels are.
sentences.zh: 你可以做个血液检测，并实际展示出你的胆固醇水平是多少。

sentences.en: And with the right medications, you can then show that your cholesterol levels are changing.
sentences.zh: 通过正确的药物治疗，你随后可以证明你的胆固醇水平正在发生变化。

sentences.en: You're saying that no similar system exists when it comes to something like depression.
sentences.zh: 你是说，在面对像抑郁症这样的问题时，并不存在类似的系统。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So one of the main neurotransmitters that's implicated in this disease model or defect model is serotonin.
sentences.zh: 因此，与这种疾病模型或缺陷模型密切相关的核心神经递质之一就是血清素。

sentences.en: There's no way to assay serotonin and give your reading where you are with respect to serotonin right now in your brain like you can with cholesterol or you can with insulin.
sentences.zh: 不像胆固醇或胰岛素那样，你无法化验血清素，然后给出一个读数，告诉你目前大脑中血清素的状况。

sentences.en: So depression involves biology, but it's not a disease in the same way that diabetes is a disease or Huntington's disease is a disease.
sentences.zh: 所以抑郁症确实涉及生物学，但它并不是像糖尿病或亨廷顿舞蹈症那样的一种疾病。

sentences.en: I mean, in that case, we know what genes are responsible, and we understand what those genes are doing and how it relates to the symptoms of this neurological disorder.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在那种情况下，我们知道是哪些基因在起作用，我们也理解这些基因在做什么，以及它如何与这种神经系统疾病的症状相关联。

sentences.en: Depression, the understanding is much more diffuse.
sentences.zh: 而对于抑郁症，这种理解要模糊得多。

sentences.en: Like, maybe it has something to do with serotonin.
sentences.zh: 比如，也许它跟血清素有关。

sentences.en: Maybe it has something to do with dopamine.
sentences.zh: 也许它跟多巴胺有关。

sentences.en: That's a very different level of understanding.
sentences.zh: 那是完全不同层面的理解。

sentences.en: Another way to think about the defect model blames depression on faulty cognition and claims that the solution is the right kind of psychotherapy.
sentences.zh: 思考缺陷模型的另一种方式是将抑郁症归咎于有缺陷的认知，并声称解决方案是正确的心理治疗。

sentences.en: But you say that the evidence doesn't fully support this explanation either?
sentences.zh: 但你说证据也并不完全支持这种解释？

sentences.en: Well, I think that all of these are valid therapies.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为所有这些都是有效的疗法。

sentences.en: So if you're struggling with depression, medications are an option, and cognitive behavioral therapy is an option.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你正在与抑郁症做斗争，药物是一种选择，认知行为疗法也是一种选择。

sentences.en: And that's a good thing to have multiple options.
sentences.zh: 拥有多种选择是一件好事。

sentences.en: But again,
sentences.zh: 但话又说回来，

sentences.en: that's very different from saying that the reason that people become depressed in the first place is because there is something fundamentally deficient in their cognition in the way that they're thinking.
sentences.zh: 这与说人们一开始会陷入抑郁的原因，是因为他们的认知或思考方式存在根本性的缺陷，是完全不同的。

sentences.en: It could be instead that these changes in cognition are part of what's maintaining the depression, which is why the therapy can be useful.
sentences.zh: 相反，有可能是这些认知的变化构成了维持抑郁的一部分，这也是为什么治疗会有用的原因。

sentences.en: So I do believe that cognitive behavioral therapies can be really helpful, not only in helping people resolve a depression episode,
sentences.zh: 所以我确实相信，认知行为疗法真的很有帮助，不仅能帮助人们走出抑郁期，

sentences.en: but the skills that are learned in cognitive behavioral therapy can be useful in keeping people well.
sentences.zh: 而且在认知行为疗法中学到的技能，对于保持人们的健康也很有用。

sentences.en: So I do believe that cognition is a contributing factor to depression.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实相信，认知是导致抑郁的一个因素。

sentences.en: But that, again, is different than saying that people who are depressed all are somehow defective or deficient in how they think about the world.
sentences.zh: 但话又说回来，这与说所有抑郁的人在看待世界的方式上都有某种瑕疵或缺陷，是两码事。

sentences.en: John's point is not that medications and psychotherapy are ineffective and should be discarded.
sentences.zh: 约翰的观点并不是说药物和心理治疗无效，应该被抛弃。

sentences.en: He thinks they have helped millions and could help millions more.
sentences.zh: 他认为它们已经帮助了千百万人，还能帮助更多的人。

sentences.en: His point is only that depression is not necessarily evidence that there is something wrong with the brain.
sentences.zh: 他的观点仅仅是，抑郁症并不一定能证明大脑出了什么问题。

sentences.en: In fact, he believes the capacity for depression is wired into the brain.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他相信大脑天生就具备产生抑郁的潜能。

sentences.en: There's no question that nature built us with the capacity for low mood.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，大自然在塑造我们时，就赋予了我们产生低落情绪的能力。

sentences.en: And once you have that capacity for low mood, you have the capacity for more serious, more severe, more long-lasting low mood.
sentences.zh: 一旦你有了产生低落情绪的能力，你也就具备了产生更严重、更深层、更持久的低落情绪的能力。

sentences.en: And so that is a very important adaptation.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常重要的适应机制。

sentences.en: Mood is what is integrating all of the inputs, both inside of your body and outside in your environment.
sentences.zh: 情绪整合了所有的输入信息，包括你身体内部的以及外部环境中的。

sentences.en: And mood is the thing that's asking the question, what should I do next?
sentences.zh: 情绪正是那个提出“接下来我该做什么？”这一问题的东西。

sentences.en: Is this environment that I'm in good for action or is it bad for action?
sentences.zh: 我所处的这个环境适合采取行动，还是不适合采取行动？

sentences.en: And so low moods are unpleasant, just as pain is unpleasant, anxiety is unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 因此，低落情绪是不愉快的，正如疼痛是不愉快的，焦虑是不愉快的。

sentences.en: But I think it's easier for people to see that pain is an evolved mechanism that allows us to protect our body from physical damage.
sentences.zh: 但我认为人们更容易理解疼痛是一种演化而来的机制，它能保护我们的身体免受物理损伤。

sentences.en: And anxiety is a mechanism that allows us to avoid threats.
sentences.zh: 而焦虑则是一种让我们能够避开威胁的机制。

sentences.en: But what is the purpose of mood?
sentences.zh: 但情绪的目的是什么呢？

sentences.en: It's harder for people to see that mood itself could have a purpose, but it actually is sharing a great amount of similarity with anxiety, with pain,
sentences.zh: 人们很难看出情绪本身能有什么目的，但它实际上与焦虑、疼痛，

sentences.en: and with other mechanisms like fever that are protecting us.
sentences.zh: 以及像发烧这样保护我们的其他机制有着极大的相似性。

sentences.en: From an evolutionary perspective, John, what do you think mood is actually doing for us?
sentences.zh: 约翰，从演化的角度来看，你认为情绪实际上在为我们做什么？

sentences.en: It's telling us, should we proceed or should we stop?
sentences.zh: 它在告诉我们，我们应该继续前进，还是应该停下来？

sentences.en: So if you think at the most basic level of a little foraging animal where it's reached a patch of grass where there are no leaves of grass to eat and everywhere it looks,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你从最基本的层面去想，比如一只觅食的小动物，它走到了一片没有草叶可吃、而且放眼望去

sentences.en: there's no leaves of grass to eat.
sentences.zh: 到处都没有草叶可吃的地方。

sentences.en: Should the organism keep moving or should the organism stop?
sentences.zh: 这个生物是应该继续前行，还是应该停下来？

sentences.en: Writ large, imagine there's a famine and there's no food available.
sentences.zh: 推而广之，想象一下发生了饥荒，没有任何食物可吃。

sentences.en: Mood is a stop mechanism.
sentences.zh: 情绪正是一种叫停机制。

sentences.en: And when we come to humans, the situations that can prompt low mood become much more complicated than threats to your physical well-being.
sentences.zh: 而当我们谈到人类时，引发低落情绪的情况要比对身体健康的威胁复杂得多。

sentences.en: They involve also your future prospects for survival and reproduction.
sentences.zh: 它们还涉及你未来生存和繁衍的前景。

sentences.en: You experience low mood when there is a dilemma and it is uncertain whether or not you should proceed or whether you should stop.
sentences.zh: 当你面临两难境地，且不确定自己是该继续前进还是停下来时，你就会体验到低落情绪。

sentences.en: And low mood forces you to think about the situation maybe longer than you would like.
sentences.zh: 低落情绪迫使你对局势进行思考，时间可能会比你想要的要长。

sentences.en: But without it, we would subject ourselves to harm and we would be moving forward rashly.
sentences.zh: 但如果没有它，我们就会让自己陷入险境，并且会轻率地向前冲。

sentences.en: I mean, think about what happens after someone dies.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，想想人死后会发生什么。

sentences.en: There's a funeral.
sentences.zh: 会有葬礼。

sentences.en: Everyone comes together.
sentences.zh: 大家聚在一起。

sentences.en: They do not feel good, but they mark this as an important moment where I have to figure out who am I and how will I continue without this person in my life?
sentences.zh: 他们感觉不好，但他们将这标记为一个重要时刻：我必须弄清楚我是谁，以及没有这个人我的生活将如何继续？

sentences.en: And I think everyone would see that grief is a natural process, an inevitable process.
sentences.zh: 我想每个人都会认为悲伤是一个自然的过程，一个不可避免的过程。

sentences.en: It's a cross-cultural process.
sentences.zh: 这是一个跨文化的过程。

sentences.en: It's even observed in other species.
sentences.zh: 甚至在其他物种身上也能观察到。

sentences.en: And it, again, like depression, is very unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 而且和抑郁一样，它也非常令人不快。

sentences.en: It's a very difficult state.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常艰难的状态。

sentences.en: So nature is not optimized for our happiness.
sentences.zh: 所以大自然并没有为我们的快乐进行过优化。

sentences.en: Nature really cares more that we survive and reproduce than that we experience joy.
sentences.zh: 比起让我们体验快乐，大自然其实更在意我们能否生存和繁衍。

sentences.en: But, you know, my depression actually fits some of these parameters in that I had invested so much in this life plan to become a historian.
sentences.zh: 不过，你知道的，我的抑郁症确实符合其中一些参数，因为我曾为立志成为一名历史学家这一生活规划投入了太多心血。

sentences.en: And that I think I sensed that I was going to have difficulty getting a job as a historian.
sentences.zh: 而我想我当时已经隐约感觉到了，我要找到一份历史学家的工作会很困难。

sentences.en: And my body was kind of saying, you're not going to pursue this.
sentences.zh: 我的身体仿佛在说，你不会再追求这个了。

sentences.en: And so I was forced to stop and reconsider kind of against my will and come up with a new life plan, which was not an easy process at all,
sentences.zh: 所以我被迫违背自己的意愿停下来重新思考，并制订了一个新的人生规划，这绝对不是一个轻松的过程，

sentences.en: but did ultimately put me on a path towards a more viable future for myself.
sentences.zh: 但它最终确实让我走上了一条通往更有可行性的未来的道路。

sentences.en: You know, we talked with Lisa Feldman Barrett at Northeastern University some time ago on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，不久前我们在《隐藏的大脑》中采访了东北大学的丽莎·费尔德曼·巴雷特。

sentences.en: And one of her interesting and provocative ideas when it comes to the world of emotions is she argues that emotions are predictions about the world rather than reactions to the world.
sentences.zh: 在情感世界方面，她有一个有趣且发人深省的观点，她认为情感是对世界的预测，而不是对世界的反应。

sentences.en: They're basically guides that tell us, go forward, seek this out.
sentences.zh: 它们基本上是指引，告诉我们：前进，去追求这个。

sentences.en: This is going to be fun, be excited, have high energy, or on the other hand, withdraw, be careful, be afraid.
sentences.zh: 这会很有趣，要兴奋起来，保持高能量；或者换句话说，退缩，小心点，害怕吧。

sentences.en: Something is dangerous here.
sentences.zh: 这里有什么东西很危险。

sentences.en: So when we think about emotions as predictors as opposed to reactions, that fits very well with your thesis that moods in some ways are a guide telling us what to do next.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们把情感视为预测器而非反应时，这与你的论点非常契合，即情绪在某种程度上是指示我们接下来该做什么的指南。

sentences.en: I completely agree with that.
sentences.zh: 我完全同意这一点。

sentences.en: What's already happened is spilled milk.
sentences.zh: 覆水难收，过去的事已经发生了。

sentences.en: From the perspective of evolution, it doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 从演化的角度来看，这并不重要。

sentences.en: To give an example, I remember 9-11 in watching the planes hit the towers, and I felt immediate terror, and I felt immediate sadness, and I felt immediate rage.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，我记得911事件中看到飞机撞击大楼时，我感到了即刻的恐惧，我感到了即刻的悲伤，我感到了即刻的愤怒。

sentences.en: But it was about the future.
sentences.zh: 但这是关于未来的。

sentences.en: It really was.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Those feelings were about the future because there were the questions about who had done this, and what would happen next, and were we safe where we were right now,
sentences.zh: 这些情绪是关于未来的，因为当时存在着这样的问题：是谁干的，接下来会发生什么，我们在当下所在的地方是否安全，

sentences.en: and whoever did this had to pay.
sentences.zh: 而且无论谁干的都必须付出代价。

sentences.en: I think that people thought that they were reacting against what had happened, but it was really the implications for the future that made those feelings so strong.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们以为他们是在对已经发生的事情做出反应，但真正让这些情绪如此强烈的是对未来的影响。

sentences.en: So I agree that our feelings are there to help us do what we need to do in the moment, and that's a future-oriented system.
sentences.zh: 所以我认同，我们的情绪存在是为了帮助我们做当下需要做的事，这是一个面向未来的系统。

sentences.en: To bear down on this just a moment longer, you told me how debilitating your depression was, how you felt like there was no end in sight.
sentences.zh: 为了再深入探讨一下这个话题，你曾告诉我你的抑郁症是多么令人虚弱，你觉得生活看不到尽头。

sentences.en: You even had thoughts of ending your own life.
sentences.zh: 你甚至有过结束自己生命的念头。

sentences.en: How could a condition that is so disabling, a condition that prompted you to consider suicide, how can this be understood as a beneficial adaptation?
sentences.zh: 一个如此致残、甚至促使你萌生自杀念头的病症，怎么能被理解为一种有益的适应机制呢？

sentences.en: Well, I think that there's many things about depression in our contemporary life that are not serving us well.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为在我们现代生活中，抑郁症有很多方面对我们并没有好处。

sentences.en: My point only is that the original adaptation is useful, not that every instance of depressed mood is useful.
sentences.zh: 我的观点仅仅是，最初的适应机制是有用的，并不是说每一次抑郁情绪的发作都是有用的。

sentences.en: And in fact, there can be mismatches between the environment in which the adaptation emerged in our current environment.
sentences.zh: 事实上，适应机制赖以出现的远古环境与我们当前的环境之间可能存在错配。

sentences.en: Another thing that I really want to bring up that is unique to humans in human depression is the power of language and what that does to depressive episodes.
sentences.zh: 我想提出的另一件对人类和人类抑郁症而言独一无二的事情，是语言的力量以及它对抑郁发作所产生的影响。

sentences.en: Because I think in an evolutionary perspective, it's important to keep in mind that this adaptation is seen across species.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为从演化视角来看，重要的一点是要记住，这种适应机制在各个物种中都能看到。

sentences.en: And so we can talk about mouse depression or dog depression.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以谈论老鼠的抑郁或狗的抑郁。

sentences.en: But my dog, I had a dog, Cyrus, and I think that there probably were times in his life when his environment was unpropitious and maybe he was depressed.
sentences.zh: 但是我的狗——我曾养过一只名叫西罗斯的狗，我想在他的生命中，可能确实有过某个时期，他的环境很不顺心，也许他也很沮丧。

sentences.en: But Cyrus did not get down on himself.
sentences.zh: 但西罗斯并没有生自己的闷气。

sentences.en: He did not say that he was failing as a dog.
sentences.zh: 他没有说自己是一只不合格的狗。

sentences.en: He didn't say that he should never have been born, right?
sentences.zh: 他并没有说他本就不该出生，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it's funny,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这很有趣，

sentences.en: but I mean this in all seriousness that these are some of the things because of our unique ability to use language and to have a self-view and a self-story that human depression can be much,
sentences.zh: 但我是极其认真地说，由于我们拥有独特的使用语言的能力、自我认知以及自我故事，人类的抑郁情绪才会变得如此、

sentences.en: much more deep and terrifying.
sentences.zh: 如此之深且令人恐惧。

sentences.en: We're using some of the tools that enabled us to differentiate ourselves from other species and have, in a sense, mastery of the entire Earth.
sentences.zh: 我们正在使用一些曾让我们区别于其他物种、并在某种程度上主宰整个地球的工具。

sentences.en: But these are some of the tools that are also used against ourselves.
sentences.zh: 但这些工具，有时也被用来对抗我们自己。

sentences.en: So, again, a perfectly good adaptation.
sentences.zh: 所以，再次说明，这是一种完全健康的适应机制。

sentences.en: But in the hands of a highly intelligent person using language, we become our own worst enemies.
sentences.zh: 但在一个高度聪明的语言使用者手中，我们反倒成了自己最糟糕的敌人。

sentences.en: So, in some ways, what I hear you saying, John, is that, you know, as you discussed, the capacity for anxiety is a good thing,
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，我听到你的意思是，约翰，正如你所讨论的，焦虑的能力是一件好事，

sentences.en: which is that it's important to be on the lookout for predators or threats.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，警惕掠食者或威胁是很重要的。

sentences.en: And in our evolutionary history, this was a very useful adaptation.
sentences.zh: 在我们的进化史上，这是一种非常实用的适应机制。

sentences.en: But in the modern world in which we live, we are inundated with stories about things that could be threatening.
sentences.zh: 但在我们生活的现代世界里，我们充斥着关于潜在威胁的故事。

sentences.en: We're reading blog posts, we're reading newspaper articles, we're watching cable television, we're on social media,
sentences.zh: 我们阅读博客文章，阅读报纸文章，看有线电视，刷社交媒体，

sentences.en: and we're constantly being told about all the threats that are in our environments.
sentences.zh: 我们不断被告知周围环境中存在着各种威胁。

sentences.en: And this natural, healthy adaptation to experience fear, to be wary of threats,
sentences.zh: 这种体验恐惧、警惕威胁的自然、健康的适应机制，

sentences.en: now gets put into hyperdrive because we're in an environment that is constantly pressing that button over and over again.
sentences.zh: 现在却被过度驱动了，因为我们身处一个不断反复按下这个按钮的环境中。

sentences.en: Is that the point that you're making?
sentences.zh: 这就是你想表达的观点吗？

sentences.en: It is the point that I'm making.
sentences.zh: 这确实是我想表达的观点。

sentences.en: And I make it a little bit different for depression because some of the environmental factors involve our culture.
sentences.zh: 我对抑郁症的看法略有不同，因为一些环境因素牵涉到我们的文化。

sentences.en: So, for example, we don't simply experience our mood.
sentences.zh: 所以，举例来说，我们不仅体验自己的情绪，

sentences.en: We also experience our mood relative to what we believe we should be experiencing or what we believe other people are experiencing.
sentences.zh: 我们体验情绪时，还会参照我们认为自己应该体验到的情绪，或者我们认为别人正在体验的情绪。

sentences.en: So,
sentences.zh: 所以，

sentences.en: this phenomenon of social media has really changed how people experience their mood because what people often project on social media are lives where I am leading an ecstatic existence of a series of amazing experiences.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体这种现象确实改变了人们体验情绪的方式，因为人们在社交媒体上经常呈现出一种过着狂喜生活、充满一系列惊艳经历的形象。

sentences.en: And if you witness other people's social media feeds, you may come to believe that other people are experiencing off-the-charts positive affect,
sentences.zh: 如果你看了别人的社交媒体动态，你可能会开始相信别人正体验着爆棚的积极情感，

sentences.en: which leads you to ask the question, why am I not experiencing this?
sentences.zh: 这就会让你产生疑问：为什么我没有这种体验？

sentences.en: So, you're experiencing a big discrepancy between what you believe you ought to be feeling and what you are feeling and what you believe other people are feeling.
sentences.zh: 因此，你所体验到的是：你认为自己应该感受到的、你实际感受到的，以及你认为别人感受到的，这三者之间存在着巨大的落差。

sentences.en: So, your mood becomes a big problem in this environment.
sentences.zh: 所以，在这种环境下，你的情绪成了一个大问题。

sentences.en: And then you start to ask the question, what is wrong with me that I feel this way?
sentences.zh: 然后你开始质问：我到底怎么了，为什么会有这种感觉？

sentences.en: And I believe that more people are asking that question right now than have ever asked that question in human history.
sentences.zh: 我相信，现在问这个问题的人比人类历史上任何时候都要多。

sentences.en: Certainly, if I think about my Russian and Eastern European peasant ancestors in the 19th century who were living in villages, I do not think that they were all the time thinking,
sentences.zh: 当然，如果我想起19世纪生活在村庄里的俄罗斯和东欧农民祖先，我不认为他们会整天都在想，

sentences.en: what is wrong with the way that I am feeling?
sentences.zh: 我现在的这种感觉到底是哪儿不对劲？

sentences.en: I think there was a greater acceptance that negative emotions perhaps were the par for the course to be expected.
sentences.zh: 我认为，当时人们对负面情绪有更高的接纳度，觉得这或许原本就是生活的一部分。

sentences.en: So, there's a number of things that are going on in our contemporary environment that are probably exacerbating low mood.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们当代环境中有许多因素，可能都在加剧低落情绪。

sentences.en: So, here again, the problem might not be social comparison per se because, again, as you point out, in our ancestral environments, perhaps some social comparison was useful.
sentences.zh: 因此，这里再次说明，问题可能本身不在于社会比较，因为正如你所指出的，在我们的祖先生活的环境中，某种程度的社会比较或许是有用的。

sentences.en: If somebody figured out how to build a better hut than your hut, then you learned to build a better hut yourself.
sentences.zh: 如果有人琢磨出了如何建造比你的茅草屋更好的房子，你就会学会自己也建一个更好的。

sentences.en: But now, we're confronted with social comparison with millions of other people, people who are better athletes, people who are eating nicer dinners,
sentences.zh: 但现在，我们要面对的是与数百万其他人的社会比较，那些更优秀的运动员，那些吃着更精致晚餐的人，

sentences.en: people who are in happier relationships.
sentences.zh: 那些处于更幸福关系中的人。

sentences.en: And we're constantly asking ourselves the question, why is it that I have fallen short?
sentences.zh: 我们不断地质问自己：为什么我就落后了？

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全如此。

sentences.en: And, you know, as opposed to the example of the hut, well, you see what the hut looks like.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，与茅草屋的例子相反，嗯，你能看清茅草屋长什么样。

sentences.en: But the truth is, we don't know what anyone is experiencing.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，我们根本不知道别人的真实体验是什么。

sentences.en: So, we're really in the dark, fundamentally, when we make these comparisons.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们进行这些比较时，基本上是处于两眼一抹黑的状态。

sentences.en: All we have are what other people say or what other people look like.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有的全部信息，只是别人说的话或别人的外表。

sentences.en: And, unfortunately, in our culture, there isn't a lot of transparency about low mood.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，在我们的文化中，对于低落情绪并没有太多的透明度。

sentences.en: People don't want to post on their Facebook profile, I'm having a low mood day.
sentences.zh: 人们不会在自己的Facebook个人资料上发帖说，我今天情绪很低落。

sentences.en: And people often don't know how to react when they do post such a thing.
sentences.zh: 而当别人真的发了这样的话时，人们往往不知道该如何反应。

sentences.en: You also observe, John, that our modern culture leads people to pursue happiness in ways that may set themselves up for unhappiness.
sentences.zh: 你还观察到，约翰，我们的现代文化引导人们去追求幸福，而这种追求方式可能会让他们陷入不幸福。

sentences.en: What do you mean by this?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, I believe in our contemporary environment, a lot of people have developed very unrealistic goals for themselves.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为在我们当代环境中，很多人为自己设定了非常不切实际的目标。

sentences.en: For example, in young people saying, I'm going to be a billionaire, or I'm going to amass 10 million followers on social media,
sentences.zh: 例如，年轻人会说，我要成为亿万富翁，或者我要在社交媒体上积聚一千万粉丝，

sentences.en: or I'm going to be the most beautiful so that I will be a fashion model and people will follow me all around the world.
sentences.zh: 或者我要成为最美的人，这样我就可以当时尚模特，人们会全世界追随着我。

sentences.en: That, unfortunately, very few people will succeed at these very unrealistic goals.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，极少有人能在这些非常不切实际的目标上获得成功。

sentences.en: And, consequently, if your happiness is contingent on reaching these goals, you will tend to feel depressed.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你的幸福取决于达成这些目标，你往往会感到沮丧。

sentences.en: Can you talk a moment, John, about how in the United States, we've actually written the pursuit of happiness into one of our foundational documents.
sentences.zh: 约翰，你能聊聊在美国，我们实际上是如何将“对幸福的追求”写进我们的奠基文献之一的吗？

sentences.en: What do you think that does to our mental states?
sentences.zh: 你认为这会对我们的精神状态产生什么影响？

sentences.en: Well, the idea of pursuing happiness obviously is very old, and you're right, Thomas Jefferson included that in the Declaration of Independence as a fundamental human aspiration.
sentences.zh: 嗯，追求幸福的想法显然非常古老，你说得对，托马斯·杰斐逊将这一点作为人类的基本诉求写进了《独立宣言》。

sentences.en: I think the question is how to pursue happiness, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为问题在于如何去追求幸福，对吧？

sentences.en: So is it that happiness is something that you experience along the way as you pursue other things that are meaningful in your life?
sentences.zh: 所以，幸福是在你追求生活中其他有意义的事情的过程中顺便体验到的东西吗？

sentences.en: So, for example, starting a family or meaningful work or helping others?
sentences.zh: 比如，组建家庭、从事有意义的工作或者帮助他人？

sentences.en: Or is happiness an end in itself, meaning I want happiness now and I need to figure out what I will do today to feel happy right now?
sentences.zh: 还是说幸福本身就是终极目的，意思是我现在就要幸福，我必须弄清楚我今天要怎么做才能立刻感到幸福？

sentences.en: Those are very different.
sentences.zh: 这两者截然不同。

sentences.en: And I think many people have started to train themselves on thinking about happiness as a short-term phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 我认为许多人已经开始训练自己将幸福视为一种短期现象。

sentences.en: And I'm not sure that Thomas Jefferson was thinking that the pursuit of happiness meant that the 18th-century farmers needed to find a way to experience euphoria today.
sentences.zh: 而且我不确定托马斯·杰斐逊当时是否认为，追求幸福意味着18世纪的农民需要找到一种方法来体验当下的狂喜。

sentences.en: Our culture has embraced the idea that depression is a sign of something broken within us.
sentences.zh: 我们的文化已经接受了这样一种观念：抑郁是我们内部某个地方出了故障的信号。

sentences.en: But John's research in affective signs suggests that depression might emerge from the same mood system that helps us to adapt and survive.
sentences.zh: 但约翰在情感科学方面的研究表明，抑郁可能源于帮助我们适应和生存的同一个情绪系统。

sentences.en: When we come back, writing a new story about depression, one that offers greater understanding and hope.
sentences.zh: 广告回来后，我们将讲述一个关于抑郁的新故事，一个能够提供更多理解与希望的故事。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔。

sentences.en: Psychologist John Rottenberg studies depression and where it comes from.
sentences.zh: 心理学家约翰·罗滕贝格专门研究抑郁症及其根源。

sentences.en: If you have a personal story about your own battles with your moods or follow-up questions or comments that you would be willing to share with the Hidden Brain audience,
sentences.zh: 如果你有关于自己与情绪抗争的个人故事，或者有愿意与《隐藏的大脑》听众分享的后续问题或评论，

sentences.en: please find a very quiet room and record a voice memo on your phone.
sentences.zh: 请找一个非常安静的房间，用手机录下一条语音备忘录。

sentences.en: Email it to us at feedback at hiddenbrain.org.
sentences.zh: 将其发电子邮件至 feedback@hiddenbrain.org。

sentences.en: Use the subject line depression.
sentences.zh: 邮件主题请写“depression”（抑郁）。

sentences.en: That email address again is feedback at hiddenbrain.org.
sentences.zh: 那个电子邮箱地址再重复一遍：feedback@hiddenbrain.org。

sentences.en: John, you say that part of your effort to push back against the defect model of depression
sentences.zh: 约翰，你说你反击抑郁缺陷模型的努力的一部分，

sentences.en: is to investigate what you call silver linings in depression and other psychological disorders.
sentences.zh: 就是去调查你所谓的抑郁症以及其他心理障碍中的“一线生机（积极面）”。

sentences.en: What do you mean by silver linings?
sentences.zh: 你所说的“一线生机”是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, historically, the idea has been that as people experience depression,
sentences.zh: 嗯，从历史上看，人们的观点一直是，当人们经历抑郁时，

sentences.en: they experience further damage.
sentences.zh: 他们会遭受进一步的损害。

sentences.en: Each episode of depression damages your relationships, damages your body, damages your mind.
sentences.zh: 每一次抑郁发作都会破坏你的关系，破坏你的身体，破坏你的精神。

sentences.en: And that leaves out the active ways that people adapt and learn from their depressive episodes.
sentences.zh: 这种观点忽略了人们从抑郁发作中进行适应和学习的积极方式。

sentences.en: And the ways that these episodes can actually be engines of meaning, engines of change, engines for a better future.
sentences.zh: 也忽略了这些发作实际上如何能够成为意义的引擎、改变的引擎、通往更美好未来的引擎。

sentences.en: And the person is actually, I hate to say it because I think many people find this difficult to accept, the better for it.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这个人会变得更好，虽然我讨厌这么说，因为我认为很多人觉得这很难接受。

sentences.en: In the course of your own depression, you learned some important things yourself.
sentences.zh: 在你自己的抑郁历程中，你自己也学到了一些重要的事情。

sentences.en: One of them is that people were really there for you.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是，人们确实一直在你身边支持你。

sentences.en: That's deeply true.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是真理。

sentences.en: I started out, I think, as a 24-year-old, laudably as an independent person.
sentences.zh: 我想我刚开始时是一个24岁、值得称赞的独立的人。

sentences.en: But I learned through my depression how much it's okay to lean on other people and that everyone gets a turn.
sentences.zh: 但通过我的抑郁经历，我懂得了偶尔依靠他人是多么没问题，而且每个人都有轮到脆弱的时候。

sentences.en: I'm wondering whether you felt greater empathy for others who've been through the same thing as a result of going through so much suffering yourself.
sentences.zh: 我在想，由于你自己经历了如此多的痛苦，你是否对那些经历过同样事情的人产生了更大的同理心？

sentences.en: I did.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And I don't think it's only me.
sentences.zh: 而且我不认为这只发生在我身上。

sentences.en: I think another, you could say, silver lining of depression is that you do develop compassion for other people's suffering.
sentences.zh: 我认为抑郁症的另一个可以说是“一线生机”的地方，就是你确实对其他人的痛苦培养出了同情心。

sentences.en: And because you have, it could be that other people are suffering for a different reason, or it may be a different variety of suffering.
sentences.zh: 正因为你经历过，其他人可能是出于不同的原因痛苦，或者可能是不同种类的痛苦。

sentences.en: But you are a little bit more attuned to that pain.
sentences.zh: 但你对那种痛苦会更加敏感。

sentences.en: And that is, in some ways, it's a good thing because it's a way that you're in touch with a part of your fundamental humanity in a deeper way.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这是一件好事，因为它让你以更深的方式重新触及了你的人性本质中不可或缺的一部分。

sentences.en: But that's not the only kind of irony of suffering.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是痛苦带来的唯一一种奇妙之处。

sentences.en: I think that also, from suffering deeply, you can come to appreciate not suffering in a more profound way, meaning that I wake up today and I'm not in pain.
sentences.zh: 我认为，同样由于经历过深深的痛苦，你会以更深刻的方式来感激“没有痛苦”的状态，这意味着我今天醒来时我没有感到痛苦。

sentences.en: And that is beautiful in a way that I don't think I could appreciate before I struggled with depression.
sentences.zh: 这种感觉是如此美好，我认为在我与抑郁症抗争之前，我是无法体会到这一点的。

sentences.en: And not to say that everyone who's going through life who hasn't experienced depression or some other mental health crisis is sleepwalking through life.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说生活中那些没有经历过抑郁或其他心理健康危机的人就是在浑浑噩噩地过日子。

sentences.en: I wouldn't say that.
sentences.zh: 我不会这么说。

sentences.en: But I do think that the experience of being depressed, of being suicidal, is something that can make you appreciate normality, if that's a phrase,
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，经历过抑郁、有过自杀倾向的体验，能让你以一种比从未有过这种经历更为强烈的方式去感激“正常”状态——如果可以这样称呼的话。

sentences.en: in a more robust way than if you hadn't had this experience in the first place.
sentences.zh: （译者注：此处接上句，即比未经历过的人更能体会到正常生活的可贵。）

sentences.en: You told me when you were describing your depression that at times it felt like it was bigger than you, that it was stronger than you,
sentences.zh: 你向我描述你的抑郁时曾说，有时它感觉比你更庞大，比你更强壮，

sentences.en: that you were dealing with a force that in some ways was much more powerful than you were.
sentences.zh: 你面对的是一种在某些方面比你强大得多的力量。

sentences.en: But at the same time, John, you are here today.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，约翰，你今天依然坐在这里。

sentences.en: Your depression isn't.
sentences.zh: 而你的抑郁症却没有。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: This is one thing that keeps me going, the knowledge that I was able to persevere.
sentences.zh: 这是支撑我坚持下去的事情之一，那就是我知道自己能够坚持下来。

sentences.en: And none of us, I hate to say, is immune from depression or even suffering.
sentences.zh: 而且恕我直言，我们当中没有人能对抑郁甚至痛苦免疫。

sentences.en: Suffering is inevitable.
sentences.zh: 痛苦是不可避免的。

sentences.en: It's really how we are able to tolerate it and work with it and hopefully integrate it into our lives that really enables us to move forward.
sentences.zh: 真正能让我们继续前行的，其实是我们如何去容忍它、应对它，并希望将其融入我们的生活。

sentences.en: There have been a number of studies that have also found that people who are experiencing depression in some ways can have a more accurate view of reality than people who are not depressed,
sentences.zh: 许多研究还发现，正在经历抑郁的人在某些方面可能比没有抑郁的人对现实有更准确的看法，

sentences.en: that when we are in a low mood, in a bad mood, sometimes we might actually be able to see ourselves, to see the situation more clearly.
sentences.zh: 当我们在情绪低落、心情不好时，有时我们实际上可能能够更清晰地审视自己、审视局势。

sentences.en: And in some ways, this aligns with your thesis that if a low mood is designed to make us stop and think and ponder,
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这与你的论点不谋而合：如果情绪低落旨在让我们停下来思考和沉思，

sentences.en: perhaps we're able to stop and think and ponder better than when we are in a euphoric mood.
sentences.zh: 那么也许我们比处于狂喜情绪中时更能好好地停下来思考和沉思。

sentences.en: It's probably true.
sentences.zh: 这很可能是真的。

sentences.en: I'm not arguing that we should all encourage ourselves to be depressed, so we'll process the world in a more accurate way.
sentences.zh: 我并不是在争辩说我们都应该鼓励自己去抑郁，这样我们就能以更准确的方式处理世界的信息。

sentences.en: But I think we should also be attuned to the ways that being in a good mood is consistent with having some, you could say, positive illusions.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们也应该关注那些与拥有某种（可以说）积极幻觉相契合的好心情状态。

sentences.en: So we temporarily suspend or put to the side big things like that we are mortal, that we are all going to die and that all the people that we care about are going to die, too.
sentences.zh: 所以我们会暂时悬置或抛开一些重大事情，比如我们会死，我们所有人都会死，我们在乎的所有人也都会死。

sentences.en: That we temporarily don't focus on the suffering and the bad news that's happening on every continent.
sentences.zh: 我们暂时不关注那些正在各大洲发生着的痛苦和坏消息。

sentences.en: And that's totally understandable in that when you're depressed, you become much more attuned to these hard truths is very much a mixed blessing.
sentences.zh: 这完全可以理解，因为当你抑郁时，你会变得对这些残酷的真相更加敏感，这绝对是福祸参半。

sentences.en: But it is something that is a part of this low mood syndrome that we think about things,
sentences.zh: 但它确实是这种低落情绪综合征的一部分，我们会思考事情，

sentences.en: we think about things deeply and that we don't look away from the pain or the painful things.
sentences.zh: 我们会深入思考事情，我们不会将视线从痛苦或痛苦的事情上移开。

sentences.en: In fact, we immerse ourselves in the pain and the difficult things.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们沉浸在痛苦和艰难的事情之中。

sentences.en: You've also indicated that in some ways, your own depression was the origin story of your research career as a psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 你也曾指出，在某种程度上，你自己的抑郁经历是你作为一名心理学家的研究生涯的起源故事。

sentences.en: In some ways, it seems odd to say this, but depression helped you find your purpose in life.
sentences.zh: 从某些方面来说，这样说似乎很奇怪，但抑郁确实帮你找到了人生的目标。

sentences.en: Oh, it definitely helped me find my purpose in life.
sentences.zh: 哦，它绝对帮我找到了人生的目标。

sentences.en: There's no question about that.
sentences.zh: 这一点毫无疑问。

sentences.en: And strange thing to say, but I think truthful thing to say is that I feel grateful that I was able to make this big change in my life,
sentences.zh: 虽然说出来有点奇怪，但我认为实话实说就是，我感到很感激，因为我能够对自己的生活做出这个重大的改变，

sentences.en: even though it was extraordinarily painful and it put me at risk.
sentences.zh: 尽管这一过程极其痛苦，并且让我置身于危险之中。

sentences.en: I think I was at grave risk for not making it to the other side.
sentences.zh: 我想我当时面临着无法挺过难关的巨大危险。

sentences.en: But I have now been on the other side for some decades, and I don't think any of this would have happened if I had continued in history.
sentences.zh: 但现在我已经走出来几十年了，而且我认为如果我沿着过去的轨迹继续下去，这一切都不会发生。

sentences.en: I want to take a moment and underline something really important.
sentences.zh: 我想花点时间强调一件非常重要的事情。

sentences.en: You've studied some of the silver linings that come with depression.
sentences.zh: 你研究了伴随抑郁而来的某些“一线生机”。

sentences.en: You've challenged the idea that depression is a brain disorder or merely about errors in cognition.
sentences.zh: 你挑战了这样一种观点，即抑郁是一种脑部疾病，或者仅仅是认知上的错误。

sentences.en: Some people might listen to this and say, okay, John Rottenberg thinks that the enterprise of treating depression with psychotherapy or medications is flawed.
sentences.zh: 有些人听到这里可能会说，好吧，约翰·罗滕贝格认为用心理治疗或药物治疗抑郁症的事业是有缺陷的。

sentences.en: This should be discarded.
sentences.zh: 这应该被抛弃。

sentences.en: That is not what you are saying, right, John?
sentences.zh: 约翰，这不是你想表达的意思，对吧？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然不是。

sentences.en: I would love for there to be less depression in the world, and I am very interested in trying to understand how people can experience well-being despite a history of depression,
sentences.zh: 我非常希望世界上少一些抑郁症，我也非常热衷于去理解，人们如何在曾有抑郁史的情况下依然体验到幸福感，

sentences.en: how people can avoid having future episodes of depression.
sentences.zh: 人们如何才能避免未来再次发作抑郁。

sentences.en: Depression is demoralizing, and it often leads people to be profoundly hopeless.
sentences.zh: 抑郁会消磨人的斗志，它往往会让人陷入深深的绝望。

sentences.en: So I am delighted to be able to say that there are treatments, and people should absolutely try psychotherapy.
sentences.zh: 所以我很高兴能告诉大家，目前是有治疗方法的，人们绝对应该尝试心理治疗。

sentences.en: They should absolutely try medications if they've found that they're not able to resolve the episode on their own.
sentences.zh: 如果他们发现自己无法靠一己之力解决抑郁发作，他们绝对应该尝试药物治疗。

sentences.en: And they should also rely, they should also try to get help from the people around them,
sentences.zh: 他们还应该依靠、应该尝试从身边的人那里寻求帮助，

sentences.en: because it often is an all-of-the-above approach that really enables people to make the kinds of changes that are needed in order to fully recover from depression.
sentences.zh: 因为通常只有采取“全方位”的方法，才能真正让人们做出必要的改变，从而从抑郁中完全康复。

sentences.en: So I believe that treatment is often a critical first step towards recovering and ultimately thriving after depression.
sentences.zh: 所以我相信，治疗通常是走向康复并最终在抑郁后繁盛的关键第一步。

sentences.en: I understand, John, that a few years ago you reached out to one of the psychiatrists who treated you when you were depressed.
sentences.zh: 我了解到，约翰，几年前你曾联系过一位在你抑郁时治疗过你的精神科医生。

sentences.en: Why did you reach out, and how did the conversation unfold?
sentences.zh: 你为什么会联系他？对话又是如何展开的？

sentences.en: I did.
sentences.zh: 是的，我联系了。

sentences.en: It was something that I thought about a lot.
sentences.zh: 这是我思考了很久的事情。

sentences.en: This was actually the psychiatrist who admitted me to the hospital at Johns Hopkins for a month, and he had been working with me for over a year.
sentences.zh: 其实这位精神科医生曾在约翰斯·霍普金斯医院让我住院一个月，他和我合作了一年多。

sentences.en: We had tried, I don't want to say everything, but we had tried many medications together and in combination, and I felt that he had done his absolute best,
sentences.zh: 我们尝试过——我不想说所有办法，但我们一起尝试了许多药物以及药物组合，我觉得他已经尽了最大努力，

sentences.en: but also that he hadn't been able to make me better.
sentences.zh: 但同时他也确实没能治好我。

sentences.en: And I felt a certain amount of guilt that I wasn't a good patient at the time, and I also felt like he didn't know me,
sentences.zh: 我当时觉得自己不是个好病人，心里有一点内疚，同时也觉得他其实并不了解我，

sentences.en: despite the fact that we had the most intimate conversations for like 18 months.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们曾进行过长达18个月左右最亲密的对话。

sentences.en: And so when I finally did recover, I thought about Dr. McGinnis, and he had become a pretty eminent research psychologist at the University of Michigan.
sentences.zh: 所以当我最终康复时，我想到了麦金尼斯医生，他当时已经成为了密歇根大学一位相当杰出的研究心理学家。

sentences.en: And I just wondered, what would it be like if I reached out to him?
sentences.zh: 我只是在想，如果我联系他会怎么样？

sentences.en: Like, would he remember me?
sentences.zh: 比如，他还会记得我吗？

sentences.en: Would he be surprised that I had not only gotten out of the depression, but that I was now in the field?
sentences.zh: 他会不会惊讶于我不仅走出了抑郁，而且现在也进入了这个领域？

sentences.en: And not only I was in the field, I was studying depression, and I was a faculty member like he was.
sentences.zh: 不仅进入了这个领域，我还在研究抑郁症，并且像他一样成为了一名教职人员。

sentences.en: And so I wrote him with really very little expectation.
sentences.zh: 因此我给他写了封信，其实并没有抱多大期望。

sentences.en: Just I really wanted to say that I knew that he had done his beSt.
sentences.zh: 我只是真的很想告诉他，我知道他当时已经尽力了。

sentences.en: He was a very kind, is a very kind man, in that it was just a really difficult depression that really I don't know if anyone could have done better than he did.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常好的人，现在也是，那是一场非常艰难的抑郁症，说实话，我不知道是否有人能比他做得更好。

sentences.en: And just see, just see what he said.
sentences.zh: 只是想看看，看看他会说些什么。

sentences.en: And not only did he write me back, he wanted to talk with me.
sentences.zh: 结果他不仅给我回了信，还想和我聊聊。

sentences.en: And we continue to be in contact, and I've seen him in person.
sentences.zh: 我们一直保持着联系，我还亲自去见了他。

sentences.en: And to me, this was very gratifying because he is someone who knew me as the depressed John, but also as the person who's on the other side of depression.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这非常令人欣慰，因为他不仅认识抑郁状态下的约翰，也认识走出抑郁之后的我。

sentences.en: And he's one of the few people who really knows all of those parts intimately.
sentences.zh: 他是极少数真正深入了解所有这些阶段的人。

sentences.en: And he also is someone who really understands depression.
sentences.zh: 而且他也是一个真正理解抑郁症的人。

sentences.en: So I think in addition to it being very gratifying for me,
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，除了对我自己很有意义之外，

sentences.en: I think it was also gratifying for him to see that his patient finally was able to get out of it and turn his life into something that is an asset to the world.
sentences.zh: 我想对他来说也很欣慰，看到他的病人最终走出了阴霾，把生活过成了一件对世界有益的事。

sentences.zh: 约翰·罗滕伯格是康奈尔大学的心理学家。

sentences.zh: 他是《深渊：抑郁症流行的进化起源》一书的作者。

sentences.zh: 约翰，非常感谢你今天来到 Hidden Brain。

sentences.en: It was such a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这真是太荣幸了。

sentences.zh: 请找一个非常安静的房间，用手机录制一段语音备忘录。
